newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi says Italy may have only one euro chance.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says Italy may have only one euro chance.

text.p: Prime minister Romano Prodi said on Thursday that Italy must make every possible effort to be a founder member of Europe's planned single currency because there might not be a second chance to join.

Speaking at a conference of retailers, Prodi said the primary aim of Italy's 1997 budget, designed to cut a massive 62.5 trillion lire ($42 billion) off next year's projected deficit, was to prepare for the single currency.
"It is to give a new balance to the public accounts, preparing for the entry to Europe with the first group of countries, which may also be the only one, looking at how things are going," he said.
Prodi said that "not being in Europe would for Italy be the end, it would mean renewed inflation and the return of a lack of rules on the economic markets." -- Rome bureau +396-678 2501
